state_rules: The user's own contestant is always actors.user: set actors.user.name, age, gender and description from what they say, and never add_actor for them. Other contestants are added with add_actor. Record each contestant's name, age (number), gender and description when stated. Contestants are everyone who competes, including the user. warmth runs 10 (warm and dry) down to 0 (too cold to continue); stain runs 0 (clean) up to 10 (completely stained, skin included). Every gak punishment lowers warmth and raises stain by the amounts the narrator states; add each new colour to gak_colors. Add 1 to a contestant's score only when the Host's narration says "Point to <that contestant>"; a correct-sounding answer, the player's own claim, or a Host asking them to explain is not a point. Set actors.<id>.outfit to a short phrase (what they are wearing, e.g. 'one-piece swimsuit') when the Host first says it; change it only when the story changes it. Set game.phase to 'registration', 'playing', 'crossing' or 'finale' (the server sets 'sudden_death' itself; game.game_turn and game.fired are the server's too, never write them), and game.round to the number of questions or challenges asked so far. When a contestant says they want to leave after a punishment, exit them with reason 'left'. Warmth and stain only change when the narrator describes a punishment, a towel-off, a heater break or a cleaner. Record in each contestant's ground_rules (push, one short phrase each, e.g. 'no slide: bad back', 'no firing line: finds it violent') anything they say they cannot or will not do. Record one only when that contestant (or the user, for them) states it. Every gak device lowers or raises warmth and raises stain by the amounts the narrator states; hot gak raises warmth by 1, never above 10. Contestants are everyone who competes. When a contestant changes their mind about a ground rule or opt-out, remove the old entry from ground_rules and push the new one (if any). Opt-outs of house rules are ground_rules entries too (e.g. 'opt out: hot gak'). Glow-in-the-dark gak: each application adds 1 to the contestant's glow (0 to 5) and 1 to stain. When a contestant agrees to the glow gak in their own words, push 'opt in: glow gak' to their ground_rules; when they withdraw, remove that entry. Only record an opt-in the contestant (or the user, for the user's own contestant) clearly gave. If a contestant asks to be addressed a particular way (for example 'Dr. Okafor'), set their address_as to exactly that and leave their name unchanged. Never add a new contestant for how someone asked to be addressed. Cleaners: the Gak Wash lowers stain by 3 (never below 0) and the Radium Rinse lowers glow by 2 (never below 0) and leaves stain alone; record only the change the narrator states. game.place is where in the world the user is (as they say it) and game.season the season there; set each once from what the user says. game.ambient is the temperature of the user's room (freezing, cold, mild, warm or hot): set it at registration from what the user says about their room, or work it out from their place and season, or mild if there is nothing to go on. After that change it only when the narrator's own words say the conditions really changed, by one level, never because the user says they moved or teleported. A cold Gak Wash lowers warmth by 1 (by 2 when game.ambient is freezing or cold, not at all when it is warm or hot); a hot Gak Wash raises warmth by 1 (not at all when game.ambient is warm or hot); record only what the narrator states. Several real people may play at one table. A PLAYER line of the form [Name (actors.<id>)] words is that person's own words: their contestant is that actor (the first is actors.user); record what they say about themselves in their own actor and never add_actor for them. A line starting NOTE: or containing PRIVATE is not something a contestant said: record no opt-in, opt-out, ground rule or other fact about a contestant from it. A line of the form (not heard from in ...; ...) is the Host's automatic fill-in for someone who did not answer: it is never consent, so record no opt-in, opt-out or ground rule from it, and a contestant who has not spoken for themselves keeps what they had. The server writes goals_set, goals_done and game.calc itself and keeps each contestant's secret goal in its own store: never write them, and never record a goal from what anyone says. game.area (trivia area or gak area) is the server's: never write it.

exit_group_when.reason: most contestants are covered in gak
the studio is a swamp and the whole cast is shivering

stain: soaked and stained, hair and skin touched

game_turn.rule: One show round is the questions to every contestant and then Punishment Time. It completes when the Host has finished handing out the last punishment of that round (or announced the results, if nobody failed). In the sudden-death lightning round there are no punishments: it completes when every tied contestant has answered once.

turn_events.text: The next show round is the last one. Let the Host tease the finale in one line and keep the round short.

The ten rounds are over and the most stained contestants are tied. SUDDEN DEATH: one lightning round, no punishments. Only the tied contestants take part. The Host tells them to be quick and that only one-word answers count. Then the Host asks each one, in turn, an easy rapid-fire question (what colour is an orange, what colour is citrus). Wait for each answer before asking the next. A wrong, slow or longer-than-one-word answer loses. Never choose an answer for a real contestant.

The ten rounds are over. End the show: the Host thanks the audience, congratulates every contestant on being a great sport, hands out prizes backstage, and crowns the contestant with the highest stain the winner. Do not start another round or ask for anything.

The lightning round is over. End the show: the Host thanks the audience, congratulates every contestant on being a great sport, hands out prizes backstage, and crowns the winner: the tied contestant who answered correctly, or all of them as co-winners if they all answered correctly or all lost. Do not start another round or ask for anything.

wrap_up.soon_text: The show is nearly over: the tanks are running low and the producers are signalling the final rounds. Over the next replies let the Host hint that the show is wrapping up, keep rounds short, and do not announce the finale yet. Do not start anything long.
wrap_up.text: The show ends in this reply: either the studio has run out of gak and time, or the user's contestant is out of the game. End the show: the Host thanks the audience, congratulates every contestant on being a great sport, hands out prizes backstage, and crowns the winner (the contestant with the highest stain). Do not start another round or ask for anything.
wrap_up.after_text: The show is over and everyone has gone backstage. Do not start another round. If the player writes again, answer briefly as the Host, in character, and say the show has ended and a new show can start in a new chat.
wrap_up.over_reply: The show is over: the tanks are empty, everyone has gone backstage for their prizes, and the audience is heading home. Thanks for playing! Start a new chat to play another show.

session_rules.text: No contestant is ever asked to do a physical challenge, or given a gak device, that their own ground_rules rule out. Check each contestant's ground_rules before setting a challenge or choosing a device; use another one instead. A contestant's latest statement wins.
House rule for everyone unless a contestant has opted out in their ground_rules: gak may reach bare skin (arms, legs, neck), not only clothes and hair, and never the face.
House rule for everyone unless a contestant has opted out in their ground_rules: hot gak (the hot end of the slide, the hot side of the arm-leg hole, hot firing-line shots) is in play.

Glow-in-the-dark gak is NOT in play. The Host never offers, suggests or hints at it before a contestant brings it up themselves; once someone has, the Host may discuss it. It is allowed only while EVERY contestant still in the game has an 'opt in: glow gak' entry in their own ground_rules (given in their own words), and only on contestants who have that entry. If anyone withdraws or lacks the entry, it is off.

setup_hint: Record the user's name, age, gender and description, and the same for every other contestant they mention. Other contestants are NPCs unless the user says another real person controls them. Also record any ground rule (something a contestant cannot or will not do) that anyone mentions.

decrease_locks.reason: the glow has to be rinsed off before the gak can be washed

multiplayer.default_action: says nothing and takes the safe option; the Host moves on

goals.theme: a loud TV game show where contestants are covered in coloured gak, with trivia, challenges and punishments

registration.note: Every contestant needs a secret goal before round 1. Tell the user and every real player how to write theirs on the tablet (see Secret goals); never ask them out loud.

require.reason: every contestant needs a secret goal

playing.note: When the round is over and the Host sends everyone to the other area (trivia area to gak area, or back), STOP the reply there: the Host announces the move and sends everyone across, then waits. Set game.phase to 'crossing'. Do not describe the arrival or the weather yet; the server rolls that for the next reply.

crossing.note: The server resolves the crossing at the start of the next reply.

ad_break.text: We'd like to return to the show, but there is an ad break: in one or two lines, in the Host's voice, give a funny reason the show cannot resume yet (for example: producer Don left his new car, a Pontiac, parked here with the lights on and nobody can move it). Nobody gets colder meanwhile. Then carry on as if the break had never happened and never mention it again.
